token.note: Present this token to the recovery application operation. Applying re-derives it and rejects a changed task file, project, or saved run instead of replaying a stale preview.

guards.detail: the task file changed only in formatting (expected digest 3a7f0c9, observed 3a8df24); the next run adopts the equivalent bytes and resumes
the branch and head match the saved baseline
the working tree matches the tree the saved run published
every retained attempt holds its saved task contract

choices.name: resume
preserves: every retained attempt, its worktree, and its result commit
verified work is never repeated: startup replays receipts and coerces retained phases
changes: the run continues dispatching and publishing after it resumes

apply.description: Start the controller; the startup recovery path applies under the repository lock.

choices.name: restore-task-file
preserves: every retained attempt and its result commit
the saved backlog contract in the run state
changes: the external formatting edit is discarded and the file returns to the saved bytes (digest 3a7f0c9d21b8e45f6c0a1d2e3f4b5c6d7e8f901a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e2f3a); no task content differs, and the next run accepts the edit as-is, so restoring is optional (AX-018)

apply.description: Checked application: restores the retained accepted bytes after re-deriving the preview token; a stale preview is refused without mutation.

choices.name: import-backlog
preserves: every retained attempt, its result commit, and the saved backlog content
changes: the equivalent bytes (digest 3a8df24835bc70a19f097ae2ff78035c5f8eefd89838cc9cff0bbeb5d188577d) become the accepted export; the content and the baseline stay unchanged (AX-018)

apply.description: Checked application: applies the edit after re-deriving the preview token; a stale preview is refused without mutation.

choices.name: discard-retained
changes: retained attempts, result commits, and the saved run would be lost

apply.description: No supported discard exists; Looper never deletes retained work through recovery.
